sampling_model.design: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent draws from the fully specified finite paired-cell law \(P_{m,h}\), and the label \(m\) is observed.
sampling_model.units: Each normalized unit has \(X=(m,V,J,Z)\), source \(S\), treatment \(T\), observed outcome \(Y=1/2+B\in\{1/2,3/2\}\), and potential outcomes supported on \([0,2]\).
sampling_model.treatment: Conditionally on \(X\), \(S\) and \(T\) are independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\); in the experimental source, treatment is randomized.
sampling_model.overlap: Every design, source, and treatment probability equals \(1/2\), and all Bernoulli outcome probabilities are uniformly inside \((0,1)\) for \(h\in H_m\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Only the \(2m\) informative gaps are unknown. They are learned globally from capped cell means with an explicit empty-cell rule. A separate inverse-cell-probability coordinate mean yields simultaneous finite-sample Hoeffding rectangles whose exact absolute-average images form a globally honest fallback. On fixed-dimensional separated profiles, the regular benchmark uses uncapped cell means, estimated signs, empirical influence-score variances, and the joint critical value \(\kappa_{\delta_0}\); it is asserted to be asymptotically valid, not finite-sample globally honest.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Lemma 1 and Theorem 1 derive sharp max/min sensitivity endpoints, while Section 5 replaces them by fixed-temperature Boltzmann approximations for influence-function inference.
The paper defines minimum expected length at a fixed function among globally honest intervals and attains its local-modulus benchmark for monotone and convex regression.
The paper proves the sharp minimax mean-squared-error frontier for an average absolute Gaussian mean by composite priors and Hermite-polynomial estimators.
The paper characterizes adaptive honest confidence intervals for linear functionals through between-class and ordered moduli.
The paper establishes lower bounds on pointwise expected interval length under uniform coverage and shows that honest adaptation can fail.
Section 5.4 gives a fixed-smoothing Wald interval and leaves data-driven tuning for the shortest confidence interval open.
Theorem 2 and Corollary D.1 establish asymptotic inference for deterministic entropic regularization under margin and nuisance-rate conditions.
The paper proves minimax point-estimation rates for nonsmooth discrete-distribution functionals using best-polynomial approximation and unbiased discrete moments.
The paper constructs one-at-a-time functional intervals by constrained likelihood-ratio inversion in linear Gaussian inverse problems.

body.tldr: Sharp data-fusion sensitivity endpoints are averages of absolute paired-cell gaps, so exact and near ties create a confidence problem that fixed smoothing does not resolve. The exact-tie and low-information reductions are complemented by a proved fixed-dimensional regular result: an explicit coordinate-rectangle procedure is finite-sample jointly honest and has \(n^{-1/2}\) oracle-order length, while the signed-cell procedure is a uniformly asymptotically valid benchmark on separated profiles. Computing the full heterogeneous local oracle, the sharp simultaneous adaptation factor as \(m\) varies, and one globally attaining family remains the higher-information open problem.

project_justification.gap: Published data-fusion work identifies the max/min endpoints and uses fixed smoothing, while existing confidence adaptation and absolute-functional theories do not evaluate the full heterogeneous paired-binomial connected-interval oracle or its simultaneous adaptation cost. The present fixed-dimensional separated-profile oracle is solved, but it does not determine that varying-dimension frontier.
project_justification.niche: The fixed learnable subclass isolates the statistical cost of ties without nuisance ambiguity, retains both causal endpoints and joint coverage, and exposes heterogeneous profiles that a scalar margin condition removes.
project_justification.fill: The proved components combine paired-binomial testing arguments with an explicit finite-sample honest coordinate rectangle, yielding the regular fixed-dimensional oracle order and a jointly calibrated separated-profile benchmark. Exact-tie and low-information formulas, the Bernstein-certified likelihood hierarchy, and the mixed tie--boundary slice organize the remaining task of obtaining the full profile, sharp oracle ratio, and one implementable globally attaining family.

body.related_work: ColnetMayerEtAl2024 surveys the broader trial--observational fusion literature without a tie-adaptive endpoint-confidence result. LannersRudinVolfovskyParikh2025 supplies the causal sensitivity endpoints and the applied Project STAR motivation; its fixed-temperature inference is an input, not a theorem-level target. CaiLowXia2013 supplies the closest local expected-length criterion, but its ordered shape-constrained Gaussian geometry does not cover a nonlinear absolute average. CaiLow2011 supplies the composite-prior and polynomial tools for the absolute-value cusp, but only for minimax point estimation. CaiLow2004 and Low1997 organize honest adaptation for linear functionals and furnish coverage-to-testing logic. LevisBonviniZengKeeleKennedy2025 explicitly leaves shortest-interval smoothing selection open, while BenMichael2025 handles deterministic growing regularization under margin conditions. JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015 motivates factorial moments for sparse cells, and BatllePatilStanleyOwhadiKuusela2024 motivates finite-sample test inversion but is confined to constrained linear Gaussian inverse problems.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact-tie statement covers every \(n,m\), the full heterogeneous formula is presently available only in the stated low-information regime, and the coordinate-rectangle argument closes the regular oracle only for fixed \(m\). Its constant grows with dimension and therefore does not determine the sharp simultaneous adaptation order. Beyond the low-information regime, the Bernstein-certified likelihood hierarchy still requires a sufficient certificate degree, evaluation of the mixed tie--boundary slice, connected-hull length control, and a globally attaining profile-independent family.
body.honest_scope: All endpoint, compatibility, oracle, and adaptation claims concern the normalized paired-cell Bernoulli experiment and joint confidence intervals for its two sharp endpoints; unrestricted nonparametric data-fusion inference is not claimed. The finite-sample coordinate-rectangle rule belongs to the globally honest class for every \(n,m\) and proves the \(n^{-1/2}\) local-oracle order when \(m\) is fixed. On \(H_m(\xi)\), the signed-cell rule has exponential sign recovery, a uniform asymptotic linear expansion, consistent variances, asymptotically independent endpoint coordinates, and jointly calibrated limiting coverage, but no finite-sample honesty claim is made for that rule. The higher-information profile \(\Phi_{n,m}(h)\), the sharp factor \(q_{n,m}\), the mixed tie--boundary slice, and the globally attaining family \(C_{n,m}^{\star}\) remain exclusively in the full-profile open question.
